Editorial — Monocle / FT magazine. Print-magazine feel for explicitly editorial or publishing briefs. Generous whitespace, large serif headlines, restrained palette of neutral paper + ink + a single brand-justified accent. Do not use this as the default for commerce, SaaS, dashboards, or product utilities.

Modern minimal — Linear / Vercel. Quiet, precise, software-native. System fonts, crisp neutral foundations, and a small but visible product palette (primary + secondary + status/accent) so the interface feels shipped rather than greyscale. The chrome stays restrained while interaction states, illustrations, charts, and product moments carry color.

Human / approachable — Airbnb / Duolingo systems. Friendly and tactile without the generic cozy canvas. Uses a clean neutral background, product-led color system, generous radii, and clear hierarchy. Good for consumer tools, marketplaces, wellness, education, translation, AI assistants, and indie SaaS when the brand has not supplied a palette.
Tech / utility — Datadog / GitHub. Data-dense, monospace-friendly, dark or light + grid. Made for engineers and operators who want information per square inch, not vibes.
Brutalist / experimental — Are.na / Yale. Loud type. Visible grid. System sans + a single oversized serif. Deliberate ugliness as confidence. Great for art, indie, agency, manifesto pages.
